skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps for generation, search, LLM calls, task tracking, and automation.
skill.summary: Run hosted inference.sh AI apps from Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
skill.author: inf-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate CLI documentation for inference.sh, but it includes confirmed remote shell installer instructions and many external infsh commands. Most hardcoded documentation links and API-key mentions are false positives, while cloud execution and Twitter/X automation remain meaningful operational risks. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote shell installer commands use curl piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell instructions with signed packages, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: CLI commands can transmit prompts, files, and task results to hosted services.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear data-sharing warnings and require confirmation before sending sensitive prompts or files to remote apps.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X app commands can create public or private account actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit review of account, action type, and final text before posting, messaging, following, liking, or reposting.

remediation.issue: Related-skills examples install additional skills through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted sources and ask for confirmation before installing related skills or modifying the agent environment.

remediation.issue: Shell completion examples write into user shell configuration paths.
remediation.suggestion: Label shell completion setup as optional and user-initiated, and avoid running hidden config writes automatically.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps with inference.sh
content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to discover and run hosted AI apps from agent workflows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical infsh CLI guidance for discovery, execution, tasks, and authentication.
actual_capabilities: Install and authenticate the inference.sh CLI for local use.
List, search, filter, and inspect available inference.sh apps.
Run hosted AI apps with inline input or saved input files.
Generate sample input files before running an app.
Track long-running tasks and save task results.
Reference app categories for image, video, LLM, search, 3D, and Twitter/X workflows.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, CLI access, and valid authentication.
Remote apps may send prompts, files, and results to external providers.
Installer examples need manual verification before use.
Twitter/X actions can affect public accounts and require careful approval.

use_cases.title: Run model experiments from the terminal
use_cases.description: Use infsh commands to find apps, prepare input, run jobs, and collect results for model testing.

use_cases.title: Create media assets with hosted generators
use_cases.description: Discover image, video, audio, and 3D apps, then run generation jobs without managing GPUs.

use_cases.title: Compare search and LLM providers
use_cases.description: Use catalog search and app details to select hosted search or LLM tools for a workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the inference.sh skill to find apps for image generation. Show the safest discovery steps before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare an infsh run for a video generation app. Generate the sample input first and explain what I must review.

prompt_templates.title: Track a long task
prompt_templates.prompt: Submit a long-running inference.sh app only after my approval. Then show how to check task status and save the result.

prompt_templates.title: Compare provider options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare available LLM and search apps for my workflow. Include authentication needs, data-sharing risks, costs to verify, and recommended commands.

output_examples.input: Find an image generation option for a product mockup.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists relevant apps, recommends one candidate, and explains the required prompt fields before execution.

output_examples.input: Run a video generation job and check it later.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for approval, submits the task, records the task identifier, and describes how to retrieve results.

output_examples.input: Choose a hosted search app for research.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares catalog matches, notes data-sharing concerns, and suggests the app detail command to confirm inputs.

best_practices: Confirm the app name, provider, input data, and expected cost before running remote work.
Use sample input files and review them before submitting prompts or files.
Require explicit approval before installation, related-skill setup, or Twitter/X actions.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts into a shell without verification.
Do not paste secrets, private files, or regulated data into remote app inputs without approval.
Do not automate posts, messages, follows, likes, or reposts without final human review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps agents use the inference.sh CLI to discover apps, run hosted AI jobs, and track results.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need inference.sh CLI access and authentication before running most app commands.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include image, video, audio, LLM, search, 3D, and utility app categories.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter or X?
faq.answer: The skill documents Twitter/X app commands. Use them only after explicit review and account approval.

faq.question: Is my data sent to remote services?
faq.answer: Yes. App runs can send prompts, files, and task data to inference.sh and selected providers.

faq.question: What should I verify before installing the CLI?
faq.answer: Verify the installer source, prefer signed packages or checksums, and avoid unreviewed curl-to-shell commands.
